correctness.rationale: For any d dividing m, reduction of the gcd stratum to primitive states modulo d is a bijection preserving zero times. U=(v,u+v) is invertible; z(d) is the projective return time for (0,1), with U^z(d)=cI for a unit c by Fibonacci matrix/Cassini identities. Every primitive zero hit lies in exactly one U^-j(0,c) with j=0..z(d)-1 and c a unit, producing exactly phi(d) distinct states at every possible first time; summing gcd strata proves all assertions including m=1 and t=0. The finite verifier independently checked 90 full moduli, 247065 pairs and 5741 strata/time cells.

value.rationale: The long-standing Fibonacci universal-zero and zero-containing-pairs problems naturally ask not only whether the next zero exists but when it first occurs. The new all-modulus histogram resolves that precise first-passage statistic, gives exact gcd-conditional uniformity, jump sizes determined by divisor ranks, and a closed mean waiting time; known A232656 totals do not answer any of these time-resolved questions. This is a natural complete distribution problem with a motivated explicit family.
